ESP.hook: After Switzerland, the most mountainous country in Europe — Madrid sits at 650m, the highest capital on the continent.
ESP.place: Most of the Iberian peninsula, Portugal down its western side, the Pyrenees sealing it off from France.

ITA.hook: The only country with two entire sovereign states inside it — San Marino in the northeast, Vatican City in the middle of Rome.
ITA.place: The boot kicking into the Mediterranean, Sicily at the toe and Sardinia out to the west.

PRT.hook: Has the oldest fixed borders in Europe, essentially unchanged since 1297 — and supplies about half the world's cork.
PRT.place: The western strip of Iberia: Atlantic on two sides, Spain on the other two.

GRC.hook: Around 6,000 islands, only about 230 of them inhabited, and nowhere on the mainland is more than 137km from the sea.
GRC.place: The southern tip of the Balkans, its islands scattered east across the Aegean toward Türkiye.

ROU.hook: Speaks a Romance language completely surrounded by Slavic and Hungarian ones — a linguistic island left behind by Rome.
ROU.place: North of Bulgaria on the Black Sea, with the Carpathians curving through its middle and the Danube delta on its edge.

BGR.hook: Grows much of the world's rose oil in the Valley of the Roses — it takes roughly 3,000kg of petals to make one kilogram.
BGR.place: South of Romania on the Black Sea, sitting above Greece and Türkiye.

SRB.hook: Became landlocked overnight in 2006 when Montenegro voted to leave — it kept the Danube and lost the sea.
SRB.place: The landlocked centre of the Balkans, touching eight neighbours.

HRV.hook: Over 1,200 islands, and a shape like a crescent — its coast is cut clean in two by a 20km strip belonging to Bosnia.
HRV.place: The crescent along the Adriatic, curving around Bosnia and Herzegovina.

BIH.hook: Has just 20km of coastline, at Neum — barely a beach, but enough to split Croatia's coast into two pieces.
BIH.place: Inside the Croatian crescent, with one narrow sliver reaching the Adriatic.

MNE.hook: Its name means black mountain, and the Bay of Kotor cuts so deep inland it is often mistaken for Europe's southernmost fjord.
MNE.place: On the Adriatic between Croatia and Albania.

ALB.hook: Over 170,000 concrete bunkers were poured across the country under Hoxha — roughly one for every eleven Albanians, and most are still there.
ALB.place: Facing Italy's heel across the Adriatic and Ionian, directly below Montenegro.

MKD.hook: Landlocked, and Lake Ohrid on its border is among the oldest lakes on Earth — roughly 1.3 million years, with species found nowhere else.
MKD.place: Landlocked in the middle of the southern Balkans, between Greece, Bulgaria, Serbia, Kosovo and Albania.

MLT.hook: The most densely populated country in the EU, on islands with no rivers and no lakes at all.
MLT.place: In the middle of the Mediterranean, about 80km south of Sicily.

CYP.hook: Divided since 1974, which makes Nicosia the last divided capital city in Europe — a buffer zone runs straight through it.
CYP.place: In the eastern Mediterranean south of Türkiye — geographically Asian, politically European.

AND.hook: No airport, no railway, and two heads of state at once — the President of France and a Spanish bishop share the job.
AND.place: High in the Pyrenees, entirely enclosed by Spain and France.

SMR.hook: Claims to be the oldest surviving republic in the world, founded in 301 — and it is completely surrounded by Italy.
SMR.place: A landlocked enclave inside northeastern Italy, up a mountain near Rimini.

VAT.hook: The smallest country on Earth at 0.49km² — the whole state fits inside a single city, with room for a garden.
VAT.place: Entirely within Rome, on the west bank of the Tiber.
